rules.message: calls launch() on a browser library, but trigger.config build.extensions has no browser extension (connect() to a remote browser needs none)
rules.fix: add the puppeteer or playwright build extension to build.extensions; for a remote browser use connect() and set runtime: "node"

rules.message: prismaExtension() is called without a mode, or sets migrate: true outside mode "legacy"
rules.fix: set mode to the one that matches the Prisma version and generator; keep migrate only in legacy mode

rules.message: uses ffmpeg (spawn or fluent-ffmpeg), but trigger.config has no ffmpeg() build extension, or fluent-ffmpeg is not in build.external
rules.fix: add ffmpeg() from @trigger.dev/build/extensions/core to build.extensions and fluent-ffmpeg to build.external

rules.message: pythonExtension() sets both requirementsFile and requirements, or pythonExtension is imported from @trigger.dev/build
rules.fix: use either requirementsFile or requirements, and import pythonExtension from @trigger.dev/python/extension

rules.message: imports a native or WASM package (sharp, re2, sqlite3 or similar) that trigger.config build.external does not list and that is not auto-detected
rules.fix: add the package to build.external in trigger.config.ts
rules.judge: Look for imports of native addons (re2, sqlite3, better-sqlite3, node-gyp-built packages) or WebAssembly packages. Most native modules are auto-detected as external; WASM packages must be listed in build.external. Confirm against trigger.config build.external, and against a deploy error such as: No loader is configured for ".node" files.

Does the project use TypeScript decorators (TypeORM, NestJS or other decorator-based code) AND does trigger.config.* lack emitDecoratorMetadata() from @trigger.dev/build/extensions/typescript, or is typescript missing from devDependencies? Flag only when that holds; a file with no decorators is not a hit.
rules.message: uses decorator syntax (typeorm, @nestjs or @Name(...)); trigger.config enables decorator metadata only through emitDecoratorMetadata()
rules.fix: add emitDecoratorMetadata() from @trigger.dev/build/extensions/typescript to build.extensions and typescript to devDependencies

good:
import { task } from "@trigger.dev/sdk";

export const hello = task({ id: "hello", run: async () => ({ ok: true }) });

rules.judge: Does this task read a non-JS file at runtime by path (json, html, sql, wasm, template, certificate or model files) that must exist in the deployed build, and is that file not matched by a build.extensions additionalFiles({ files }) glob in trigger.config.*? If the path is relative to process.cwd(), also check that legacyDevProcessCwdBehaviour is false. Flag only when the file is missing from the build; files pulled in through an import are bundled and do not count.
rules.message: reads a non-JS file at runtime by path; trigger.config additionalFiles may not copy that file into the build
rules.fix: add the file or glob to additionalFiles({ files }) in build.extensions and set legacyDevProcessCwdBehaviour: false

rules.message: .trigger is not listed in .gitignore, or trigger.config.* is outside the tsconfig include
rules.fix: add .trigger to .gitignore and include trigger.config.* in the tsconfig include

rules.message: @trigger.dev/build is listed under dependencies, not devDependencies
extraCACerts is set to a path that does not start with "./"
rules.fix: use a path relative to the project root that starts with ./

rules.message: additionalPackages lists a package without a version
rules.fix: pin an exact version, for example name@X.Y.Z

rules.message: trigger.config sets a literal value for a secret-looking name (syncEnvVars entry or a *_SECRET, *_TOKEN, *_PASSWORD or *_KEY key)
rules.fix: read the value from process.env or the secret store instead of a literal
